claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion capsule is scheduled to splash down on Friday, April 10, 2026, at approximately 5:07 p.m. PDT (8:07 p.m. EDT).
During Artemis II reentry, the capsule will reach 24,000 mph.
The Artemis II capsule will slow via parachutes to about 20 mph.
U.S. Navy will assist in Artemis II recovery.
During Artemis II reentry, the capsule will travel at approximately 24,000 mph (roughly Mach 32).
During Artemis II reentry, temperatures on the heat shield will reach thousands of degrees.
Artemis II reentry will result in a ~6-minute communication blackout.
The U.S. Navy and NASA personnel will lead Artemis II recovery efforts.
USS John P. Murtha will be used to retrieve the Artemis II capsule and crew.
The Artemis II crew consists of Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen.
During Artemis II descent, at roughly 6,000 feet, main parachutes will deploy to slow the capsule to approximately 20 mph before splashdown.
Heat shield damages were observed after the uncrewed Artemis I mission.
NASA modified the reentry trajectory for Artemis II following heat shield damages from Artemis I.
Live coverage of the Artemis II return will be available on NASA+, the NASA app, and the official NASA YouTube channel starting at 6:30 p.m. EDT on April 10, 2026.
